title: Grateful Dead Live at Greek Theatre, U. Of California on 1982-05-21
lineage: Sbd Mcassette > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Stellar soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1982 Greek run featuring smoking Bertha > Greatest and a legendary Playin' > Uncle John’s sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as one of the clearest early‑80s soundboard tapes, with crisp mix and excellent instrument separation. Musically the show is celebrated for its relentless energy, tight transitions and standout moments – especially Bertha into Greatest, the Playin' > Uncle John’s jam, Bird Song and a soaring Sugar Magnolia. A few listeners note that the second night edged this performance out, but overall the consensus is that this concert epitomizes the “just exactly perfect” 1982 Greek era.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (10 out of 13) are 4‑5 stars and specifically praise both the musical performance and the soundboard quality; only a single low‑rating comment is unrelated, yielding an overall strong positive consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multiple reviewers call the tape “stellar”, “crisp” and comparable to the best late‑70s recordings. No drop‑outs or balance issues are mentioned; the mix is clean with clear instrument separation.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers highlight the tight transitions, especially the seamless flow from Playin' into Uncle John’s and the well‑structured second set with a strong drum/space segment.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his soaring leads – “higher mobility” on Bird Song, “smoking” jams on Playin' > Uncle John’s and Big River, and a crisp, youthful vocal tone.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for a powerful “Philness” during the duel in the Space/Drums segment and for locking in tightly with Jerry’s improvisations.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned for an unexpected solo at the end of Uncle John’s jam; otherwise his rhythm work is described as solid throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (organ) is called “quite active” during Playin' and provides a strong backbone on the second‑set numbers.
band_member_comments.Drums: Both Bill and Mickey receive kudos for tight timing, dynamic percussion in the drum solo, and even stage antics (microphone placement, motorcycle later in the run).
